Scenario: Your CEO tweeted "our croissants beat therapy" at 3 a.m.
OptionC: Post a formal apology on LinkedIn
FeedbackA: Too late: 40 screenshots are already circulating.
FeedbackB: The hashtag trends all morning!
FeedbackC: Nobody asked for an apology. Now everyone is confused.

Scenario: A delivery drone drops a croissant on a famous food critic's head.
OptionA: Send her a free box every week for a year
FeedbackA: She writes: "Assault by pastry, but delicious."
FeedbackB: The internet does not buy it.
FeedbackC: The video reaches 3 million views. You are the villain.

Scenario: A cat influencer with 2 million followers wants to review your croissants.
FeedbackA: The cat licks one croissant. Sales explode.
FeedbackB: The cat sniffs the box and leaves. Polite success.
FeedbackC: The owner posts a sad video. Cat lovers are furious.

Scenario: Your AI-generated ad shows a hand with six fingers holding a croissant.
OptionA: Pull the ad and redo it
OptionB: Lean into it: "Six fingers, twice the croissants"
OptionC: Say nothing and hope nobody counts
FeedbackA: Safe, clean, expensive.
FeedbackB: People love brands that laugh at themselves.
FeedbackC: Everybody counts. Memes everywhere.

Scenario: A 1-star review: "My croissant arrived by drone. I wanted it by hand."
OptionC: Explain that drones are the future
FeedbackA: Your reply gets more likes than the review.
FeedbackB: The customer is happy, nobody else notices.
FeedbackC: You sound like a robot. A grumpy one.

Scenario: Competitor Baguette Bullet launches drones twice as fast as yours.
OptionA: Start a price war: -30% on everything
OptionB: Make an ad mocking their drones
OptionC: Film your bakers at 4 a.m.: quality over speed
FeedbackA: Customers love it. Your accountant cries.
FeedbackB: People find it petty.
FeedbackC: The video is beautiful. Butter, flour, sunrise.

Scenario: Black Friday is coming.
OptionC: Skip it: "we bake, we don't discount"
FeedbackA: Orders explode, quality drops, reviews too.
FeedbackB: Sold out in two hours.
FeedbackC: A few people respect that. Quietly.

Scenario: A TikTok trend: people try to catch your croissants mid-air from the drones.
FeedbackA: Best catch wins a year of croissants. Huge buzz.
FeedbackB: Responsible. Slightly boring.
FeedbackC: TikTok does not even reply. Everyone else laughs.

Scenario: A data breach: 5,000 customer addresses have leaked.
OptionB: Notify everyone and fix your security
OptionC: Notify everyone, fix it, and offer a free croissant
FeedbackA: Journalists disagree. Loudly.
FeedbackB: Painful, but people trust you a bit more.
FeedbackC: The best apology is warm and buttery.

Scenario: An intern posts a meme on the official account by mistake. 300,000 likes.
OptionB: Promote the intern to Chief Meme Officer
FeedbackA: Fans want the meme back.
FeedbackB: The intern is now more famous than your CEO.
FeedbackC: Mysterious. It works, sort of.

Scenario: A celebrity is photographed eating one of your croissants.
FeedbackA: Some people notice. Nice.
FeedbackB: Expensive, but your logo is now on prime time TV.
FeedbackC: Clever and cheap. Marketing at its best.

Scenario: Drone battery failure: 200 Sunday orders lost.
OptionB: Refund everyone and post an apology video
FeedbackA: It was sunny. Everyone checked.
FeedbackB: Honest, human, appreciated.
FeedbackC: The others complain about that too.

Scenario: Your Google Ads campaign has a 0.3% CTR and is burning cash.
OptionA: Double the budget, it will pick up
OptionB: Pause it and rewrite the ads
OptionC: Move the budget to Instagram Stories
FeedbackA: It did not pick up.
FeedbackB: Better ads, smaller bill.
FeedbackC: Croissants look better in vertical video.

Scenario: A newspaper asks: are drone-delivered croissants bad for the planet?
OptionC: Run an ad full of trees and sunsets
FeedbackA: The headline writes itself.
FeedbackB: Transparency wins you serious respect.
FeedbackC: Greenwashing detected in 12 minutes.

Scenario: A fan draws a croissant-shaped drone. The drawing goes viral.
OptionA: Share it and credit the artist
OptionB: Buy the design to sell T-shirts
FeedbackA: The artist is thrilled. So are your fans.
FeedbackB: The T-shirts sell out. The artist gets paid.
FeedbackC: You just attacked a fan. Bad idea.

Scenario: A traditional bakery accuses you of killing small bakeries.
FeedbackA: You hold your ground. Nobody really wins.
FeedbackB: Your drones now deliver their bread too.
FeedbackC: Silence looks like guilt.

Scenario: Your newsletter typo: "Fresh croissants, delivered by drunk".
OptionB: Follow-up: "Our drones are sober, we promise"
FeedbackA: Fine. Forgettable.
FeedbackB: Best open rate of the year.
FeedbackC: Some customers are now worried about the pilots.

Scenario: An investor wants you to use cheaper butter.
OptionC: Test it secretly on one product
FeedbackA: Customers taste the difference within a week.
FeedbackB: The investor leaves. Your fans cheer.
FeedbackC: A food blogger finds out. Butter-gate begins.

Scenario: A video shows a pigeon riding one of your drones.
FeedbackA: Captain Pigeon gets his own merch line.
FeedbackB: Serious. Responsible. Zero likes.
FeedbackC: The pigeon flies away. So does the buzz.

Scenario: An agency offers 50,000 fake followers for 500 EUR.
OptionC: Report the agency to the platform
FeedbackA: A journalist spots the fake accounts.
FeedbackB: Integrity costs nothing today.
FeedbackC: You get a thank-you note and some press.

Scenario: Valentine's Day is next week.
FeedbackA: Couples love them. Instagram loves them more.
FeedbackB: Singles everywhere feel seen.
FeedbackC: Just another Tuesday.

Scenario: A neighborhood complains about drone noise.
OptionC: Give every neighbor a free croissant
FeedbackA: Now they complain at 2 a.m.
FeedbackB: Silence is golden. And expensive.
FeedbackC: Complaints turn into orders.

Scenario: A LinkedIn guru calls you "the Uber of pastries".
OptionB: Invite him to visit the bakery
OptionC: Reply: "We're more the croissant of croissants"
FeedbackA: Your mum likes the post.
FeedbackB: He posts 14 selfies with flour on his face.
FeedbackC: Nobody understands. Everybody shares.

Scenario: Your website crashes during a live TV mention.
OptionA: Blame your host on social media
OptionB: Put up a "Rocket refueling" page with a promo code
FeedbackA: Customers don't care whose fault it is.
FeedbackB: The waiting page goes viral.
FeedbackC: Back online. Moment missed.

Scenario: A customer had an allergic reaction: the allergen is missing from your product page.
OptionA: Update the labels and call the customer
FeedbackA: Fast, caring, fixed.
FeedbackB: There was no small print. Disaster.
FeedbackC: Safe, but customers miss it.

Scenario: A comedian posts a parody of your latest ad.
OptionA: Ask for it to be removed
OptionB: Share it and thank the creator
OptionC: Hire the comedian for your next ad
FeedbackA: The Streisand effect: now everyone has seen it.
FeedbackB: Good sport! Your followers love it.
FeedbackC: The new ad is the funniest of the year.

Scenario: Supplier delay: no almonds for a week.
OptionA: Sell plain croissants as almond ones
OptionB: Announce an "almond-free week" with a discount
OptionC: Launch a "mystery croissant" of the day
FeedbackA: Customers notice. Of course they notice.
FeedbackB: Honest and kind of charming.
FeedbackC: People love surprises.

Scenario: A rival posts fake bad reviews about you.
OptionA: Post fake good reviews in return
FeedbackA: Now both brands look terrible.
FeedbackB: The platform removes the fake reviews.
FeedbackC: You win. Eventually. Expensively.

Scenario: A radio show wants your CEO live at 6 a.m.
OptionB: Send the head baker with fresh croissants
FeedbackA: He falls asleep live on air.
FeedbackB: The hosts eat live. Pure radio gold.
FeedbackC: They invite Baguette Bullet instead.

Scenario: End of quarter: the board wants growth, now.
OptionB: Referral program: bring a friend, get a croissant
FeedbackA: Growth, yes. Profit, no.
FeedbackB: Customers become your sales team.
FeedbackC: Revenue up, love down.

Scenario: You realize you need more marketing education to keep up with your job.
FeedbackA: You become 10 times more professional.
FeedbackB: You barely make ends meet.
FeedbackC: Nice, but not the best.

Scenario: A storm blows three drones off course. Croissants land on a wedding.
OptionA: Send a drone with champagne and apologies
OptionC: Say: "not our fault, it was the weather"
FeedbackA: The couple posts: best wedding ever.
FeedbackB: Some laugh, some want a refund.
FeedbackC: The bride replies with 4,000 words. Nobody likes you.

Scenario: Your best drone pilot quits and joins a rival, taking the route map.
OptionA: Offer a big raise to bring him back
OptionB: Launch a Pilot Academy series and train new pilots
OptionC: Post an angry thread about him
FeedbackA: He stays, but now everyone asks for a raise.
FeedbackB: The series gets 500,000 views. New pilots sign up.
FeedbackC: The thread backfires. You look petty.
